hints: controller SSD1306 (block diagram 1.6); commands per the SSD1306 technical manual (4.1)
logic supply VDD 1.65–3.3 V, absolute maximum 4 V; VIH ≥ 0.8 VDD, VIL ≤ 0.2 VDD: the interface runs at VDD, which should equal the MCU's I/O voltage (3.2, application notes)
I2C: BS0/BS1/BS2 = 0/1/0, D0 = SCL, D1 and D2 tied together as SDA, R/W# and E/RD# to VSS; 7-bit address 0x3C, 0x3D with D/C# at VDD; clock cycle ≥ 2.5 µs (400 kHz) (1.5, 3.3.5)
internal DC/DC: VBAT 3.5–4.2 V, VCC 7.0–7.5 V generated, flying capacitors between C1P–C1N and C2P–C2N; without it: VBAT to VDD, VCC 8.5–9.5 V from outside, C1P…C2N floating (1.5, 3.2)
power-up: VDD (and VBAT), display off, initialise, clear, then VCC, 100 ms, display on; power-down in reverse – VDD never off before VCC/VBAT; VCC/VBAT floating (not grounded) when off (4.2, note 13)

the data sheet asks for an electronic switch in the panel supply (VBAT) on the main board, otherwise leakage current ('Special Tips' of the application examples 3.3.4.2 and 3.3.5.2; P-/N-MOSFET pair Q1/Q2 there)
operating current: IDD ≤ 300 µA, IBAT ≤ 32 mA with the DC/DC (VDD 2.8 V, all pixels on), ICC ≤ 15 mA with external VCC 9 V (3.2)

2026-10-31: configs i2c and spi4 from the Wisevision specification Ver. A, 1.5 (BS0–BS2 table: I2C 0/1/0, 4-wire SPI 0/0/0; D0 SCL/SCLK, D1 SDIN or SDA with D2; R/W#, E/RD# and unused data pins to VSS) – the I2C address only in i2c
open: VBAT and VCC ranges depend on whether the internal DC/DC is used: only their absolute maxima are pin limits, the operating ranges are hints; VCC is typed passive because it is a supply input in one mode and the DC/DC's output in the other
charge-pump capacitors between C1P–C1N and C2P–C2N: needs has no form for a capacitor between two pins
no input voltage limit relative to VDD is given (vin_rel_max_v stays out); the SPI and parallel timing and the interface frequency depend on the mode (no single f_max_hz)
D0–D2 carry no sda/scl roles because their function depends on BS0–BS2; the address names its bus pin (on: 19); REQ.missing's I2C pull-ups follow from nets named SDA/SCL
